chapter_theme: The six adharas: the lotuses of four to sixteen petals rising from the root carry the fifty letters, and purifying them cleanses the nadis and the body; above them, through the sixteen kalas to the end of nada, the supreme Shakti stands and pure knowledge turns into the bliss of Siva.
structure_note: The petal counts from the root (1704); the ascent beyond the adharas to Shakti and the Lord (1705, 1706, 1707); purification and the body (1708); the fifty letters and the six ends in every body (1709, 1710); the sixteen-petalled flower where knowledge becomes bliss (1711). The petal counts of 1704 (4, 6, 10, 12, 16 and 2) add to fifty, the number of letters in 1709 and 1710, as the tradition matches them.

1704.reading: Four, six, ten and twelve, the sixteen marks standing above, and the first two: seeing them from the root upward and reaching their end, one may see the feet of the one who has seen time.
1704.nuance: The numbers (நாலும் இருமூன்றும் ஈரைந்தும் ஈராறும் ... பதினாறும்) are traditionally the petals of the lotuses from the root (மூலம்) to the throat, with முதல் இரண்டும் as the two petals at the brow. கோவிமேல் is obscure. காலம் கண்டான் may be Siva who mastered time (or Death), or a form of காலகண்டன், the dark-throated one.

1705.reading: Beyond the twelve of nada and at the end of the sixteen, from medha up to the end of nada, the supreme Shakti stands above, and in the changeless abode of knowing is the truth that lies above the adharas.
1705.nuance: மேதாதி நாதாந்தம் and ஈரெட்டு are taken in mantra-yoga as the sixteen kalas of the ascent above the brow, from medha to the end of nada; ஈராறு may be the twelve-finger span above the head. போதாலயம் (abode of knowing) and the third line's division are unclear, and the line may be corrupt.

1706.reading: When one sees without the two, above and below, and without the sixfold nature of 'he' and 'I', the Supreme of supremes, spread over all the earth, stands as a wishing tree, generous as a rain cloud.
1706.nuance: மேல், கீழ் may be the upper and lower centres or high and low in general; தன்மைகள் ஓராறு (six natures) may be the six adharas or six marks of the ego, and தான், நான் set the self against the other. கார் ஒன்று கற்பகம் joins the wishing tree to the rain cloud, both images of giving without stint.

1707.reading: Purifying the adharas cleanses the nadis, and with the light of the sky reached beyond the sixteen kalas from medha, the senses, the instruments and the intellect lose their ordinary working in the abode of knowing: this is the companion's path.
1707.nuance: சகமார்க்கம் (the path of the companion) is the traditional name of yoga as the third of the four Saiva paths. சாதாரணம் கெட்டான் may mean the senses lose their common working, or that the yogi loses what is common to ordinary people. The verse recurs as 1492.

1708.reading: Rousing Om without pause from medha onward, purifying the adharas and the paths, and practising until the dross in the bodily elements is driven out, the body itself becomes the fruit the adharas yield.
1708.nuance: அத்துவா are traditionally the six paths of Saiva cosmology (of mantra, word, letter, world, tattva and kala). தாது ஆர மாசு may be impurity filling the bodily elements or a reference to semen. The last line, ஆதாரம் செய் போகம் ஆவது காயமே, can mean the body is the fruit of the practice, in the spirit of Tirumular's teaching on perfecting the body, or that the body is what the adharas serve.

1709.reading: The six ends meet in every body, so mark the adharas that have been taught: above the fifty letters set in them, in the adhara where it wells up, stands the one letter.
1709.nuance: ஆறந்தம் is traditionally a set of six 'ends' (vedanta, siddhanta, nadanta and others). The fifty letters of the alphabet are distributed in tradition over the petals of the adharas, and ஓரெழுத்து (the one letter) is usually taken as Om. ஆறிய (settled, or cooled) is unclear.

1710.reading: However the body that forms, the body that perishes and the body that departs are joined together, the fifty letters, which are tattvas, are the six ends even for the body that is coming to be.
1710.nuance: The three bodies may be the gross, subtle and causal bodies, or the body born, the body dying and the subtle body that goes on. The verse makes the letters the stuff of every body; how its two halves connect is not clear from the Tamil.

1711.reading: On the lovely flower above the one that is sought are sixteen petals, and there pure knowledge becomes the bliss of Siva and ripens into abiding knowledge.
1711.nuance: A sixteen-petalled lotus is traditionally the throat centre, though the sixteen may be the kalas above the brow named in 1705 and 1707. ஆயும் may mean examined, chosen or fine. The verse recurs as 2359, which ends with the Lord joining (புணர்ந்திருந்தானே) where this ends with knowledge ripening (விளைந்தது).

links.note: The same verse appears twice. 1492's last line reads சாதா ரணங்கெட லாஞ்ச மார்க்கமே, which supports reading 1707's as 'this is the companion's path' (சகமார்க்கம்) rather than a statement about one person.

Nearly the same verse in a later tantra: the sixteen-petalled flower and pure knowledge becoming Siva's bliss. 2359 ends with the Lord united there, 1711 with knowledge ripening, so the second differs in who is the subject.

1704 counts the petals of the centres from the root upward (மூலம் கண்டு) and says that reaching their end one may see the feet of the one who has seen time (காலங்கண்டான் அடி). Song 188 asks that the breath, driven from the root up the pillar through the six centres (பாலங்கிளர் ஆறு), reach the Supreme's feet (பராபர பாதம்) in Jnana Sadasiva. Both chart the same ascent through the centres and end it at the Lord's feet.

1705 places the supreme Shakti above the sixteen kalas from medha to the end of nada (மேதாதி நாதாந்தம்). 709 joins Parai above (மீதான தற்பரை) as the sixteen kalas from medha rise (மேதாதி ஈரெண் கலை), and calls the light above the yoga of bliss. Both use the same series and set the same goal above it, Shakti or Parai, at its top.

1706 says that when one sees without the two, above and below, and without the natures of 'he' and 'I' (தான்என்றும் நான்என்றும்), the Supreme stands as a wishing tree. 1441 reports searching out 'I' and 'He' (நானென்றும் தானென்றும்) and reaching the state where there are not two. 1706 adds what follows the end of that division: the Lord gives like a rain cloud (கார்ஒன்று கற்பகம்).

1708 ends with practice purging the dross of the bodily elements so that the body itself is the fruit of the adharas (ஆதாரஞ் செய்போக மாவது காயமே). In 724 Tirumular learns the means of nurturing the body (உடம்பை வளர்க்கும் உபாயம்) because if the body perishes true knowledge cannot be won. On the reading that 1708 makes the perfected body the goal, it names one of the means 724 leaves unnamed.

1709 says the fifty letters are set in the adharas and above them, where it wells up, stands the one letter (ஓரெழுத்து). 965 says the fifty letters are all the Vedas and Agamas, and that once one knows what they become they go and become the five letters (அஞ்செழுத்து). Both reduce the fifty letters to fewer; 965 to the five syllables, 1709 further to one letter above them in the body.

source_issues: 1704: கோவிமேல் (line 2) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1705: line 3 (போதா லயத்துஅ விகாரந்தனிற்போத) is hard to divide and may be corrupt.
1707 repeats 1492 with a different last line (சாதா ரணங்கெட்டான் தான்சக மார்க்கமே against 1492's சாதா ரணங்கெட லாஞ்ச மார்க்கமே) and காலந்தத்து for கலாந்தத்து in line 2; 1492's readings look sounder.
1711 repeats 2359 with small differences in lines 1, 3 and 4.
